data.title: Turn a successful task into a tested skill
data.summary: Capture a repeatable workflow with clear inputs, deliverables and failure checks before sharing it.

facts.text: Skills package instructions and optional resources. ChatGPT and Codex load them on demand; a plugin is a distribution bundle that can also include connected tools.

prerequisites: Access to ChatGPT skill creator or Codex; check account, client and workspace availability.
A successful example, its inputs, outputs and observed failure cases.
steps: Find an existing equivalent skill or plugin before creating one.
Use the skill creator to describe the focused task, trigger, input contract and finished output.
Keep instructions portable; add scripts or templates only if the task needs them.
Run a realistic case and an incomplete-input case. Compare actual output to the expected result.
Revise based on failures and record version, owner and review date. Package for the intended host only after testing.
data.output: a reviewed skill folder and test receipt
validation: Extend or reuse it instead of installing a second ambiguous copy.
Report the missing prerequisite without claiming access was granted.
limitations: Sintra-authored procedure based on provider documentation or demonstrations; no execution in the named app was performed.
Availability and results depend on your inputs, enabled tools and permissions; a suggested practice result is not a measured outcome.
data.prompt: Find any existing skill/plugin for [repeatable task] first. Reuse or extend it when appropriate. From [successful example], create a focused instruction-only skill with a clear trigger, input contract, output format and meaningful failure checks. Keep secrets out and add scripts only if needed. Test [normal case] and [missing-input case], report actual results, then revise the draft. Explain the supported host and distribution path; do not install it or connect services as part of drafting.
tips: Include a failure example that changes the agent’s decision.
Do not embed credentials in instructions or example files.

practice.task: Capture a weekly update skill using three synthetic completed tasks and one unresolved blocker.
practice.expected: The update preserves the blocker, distinguishes shipped work from plans and does not invent owners.
